name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press (Squeeze Press)
description: Dumbbells pressed together throughout — the inward squeeze keeps the pecs under tension at lockout.

name: Dumbbell Clean and Press
description: Floor to overhead with dumbbells — the least technical whole-body lift that still builds real power.

name: Farmer's Carry
description: Heavy dumbbells, tall posture, walk. Reps field = metres.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Snatch
description: Floor to overhead one-handed. All the power of a snatch with almost none of the technique.

name: Suitcase Carry
description: One heavy dumbbell, walk without leaning. Anti-lateral-flexion loaded. Reps = metres.

name: Accomplished Pose
description: Cross-legged with one heel drawn in close, spine stacked. A steadier seat than Sukhasana for long sits.

name: Ananta’s Pose
description: Lying on one side, head propped on a hand, the top leg lifted and held. Balance on the side body while a hamstring lengthens.

name: Archer Pose
description: Seated, one foot drawn to the ear like a bowstring while the other leg stays straight.

name: Bharadvaja’s Twist
description: Legs folded to one side, torso turning to the other. The gentlest seated twist — good when a deeper one is not available.

name: Big Toe Pose
description: Standing fold holding the big toes, drawing the chest toward the shins on an inhale. A more active Uttanasana.

name: Boat Pose
description: Balanced behind the sitting bones, shins parallel or legs straight. The lower back must stay long or it is not the pose.

name: Bound Angle Pose
description: Soles together, knees wide. Hips before knees — let the thigh bones rotate rather than pressing the knees down.

name: Bow Pose
description: Face down, ankles held, kicking the shins back into the hands. The legs open the pose; the arms only hold on.

name: Bridge Pose
description: Feet hip-width, hips lifted, shoulders rolled under. Glutes and hamstrings hold while the front of the hips opens.

name: Camel Pose
description: Kneeling, hips forward over the knees, hands to the heels. The stretch is the whole front of the body, not the lower back.

name: Cat-Cow Pose
description: On all fours, alternating full spinal flexion and extension with the breath. Segment by segment, not one hinge at the waist.

name: Chair Pose
description: Sit back as if into a chair, arms overhead, weight in the heels. An isometric squat with an overhead hold on top.

name: Child’s Pose
description: Knees wide or together, hips to heels, forehead down. The reset between anything harder.

name: Cobra Pose
description: Low chest lift with the hips down and very little push from the hands. The spinal extensors do the lifting.

name: Corpse Pose
description: Lying flat, entirely still, doing nothing at all. It carries NO muscle map on purpose — no muscle is working or lengthening, which is the pose.

name: Cow Face Pose
description: Knees stacked, arms clasped behind the back one up and one down. Outer hip and shoulder rotation at the same time.

name: Crane Pose
description: Knees onto the backs of the upper arms, feet lifted, gaze forward. Rounding the upper back is the pose, not a fault.

name: Crocodile Pose
description: Face down, forehead on stacked forearms, legs loose. A prone rest that teaches the breath into the back of the ribs.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
description: An inverted V: hips high, heels reaching down, arms straight. The resting pose of a vinyasa and a full posterior-chain stretch.

name: Durvasa’s Pose
description: Standing with one leg behind the neck. A very advanced hip demand — approach through Eka Pada Sirsasana, not directly.

name: Eagle Pose
description: Legs double-crossed, arms wrapped and lifted. Squeezes the hips shut while opening between the shoulder blades.

name: Ear-Pressing Pose
description: Plough with the knees bent to the floor beside the ears. Deep spinal flexion — a strong stretch, not a strength pose.

name: Easy Pose
description: Simple cross-legged sitting, hips above the knees if a block or blanket helps. The default seat for breathing and meditation.

name: Eight-Angle Pose
description: Legs threaded around one arm and crossed, torso lowered to horizontal. A twist, a squeeze and a Chaturanga at once.

name: Eight-Limbed Salutation
description: Knees, chest and chin down with the hips lifted. The gentler alternative to Chaturanga in a beginner salutation.

name: Extended Hand-to-Big-Toe Pose
description: Standing, one leg lifted and held straight. Active hip flexion against a hamstring stretch on the same leg.

name: Extended Side Angle
description: Front knee bent, forearm to thigh or hand to floor, top arm over the ear — one line from the back heel to the fingertips.

name: Feathered Peacock Pose
description: Forearm balance. Easier on the wrists than a handstand and much harder on the shoulders.

name: Fire Log Pose
description: Shins stacked one directly above the other, ankles flexed. Blunt, honest outer-hip work — support the top knee if it floats.

name: Firefly Pose
description: Seated on the upper arms with both legs straight out to the sides. Gated by hamstrings, not by strength.

name: Fish Pose
description: Lying back on the elbows or the crown, chest lifted. Traditionally the counter-pose to Shoulderstand.

name: Four-Limbed Staff Pose
description: The bottom half of a push-up, held: elbows in at 90°, shoulders never below the elbows. The most-rushed pose in yoga.

name: Garland Pose
description: Deep squat, elbows inside the knees, heels down if they will go. Ankles, hips and lower back in one shape.

name: Gate Pose
description: Kneeling on one leg with the other extended sideways, bending over it. A clean side-body stretch with no balance demand.

name: Half Boat Pose
description: Boat lowered until the shoulders and feet hover just off the floor. Much harder than the full pose and far less flattering.

name: Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
description: Seated twist with one knee crossed over. Rotate from the mid-back and keep both sitting bones down.

name: Half Moon Pose
description: Standing on one leg with the other lifted parallel to the floor, chest open. The standing hip does nearly all of it.

name: Half Standing Forward Bend
description: Fingertips down, spine long and flat, gaze forward. The half-lift that stops the salutation being one long round back.

name: Handstand
description: Stacked over the hands, ribs in, legs together. Practise it at a wall long before practising it away from one.

name: Happy Baby Pose
description: On the back, knees to the armpits, holding the outer feet. Supported by the floor, so the lower back can let go.

name: Head-to-Knee Forward Bend
description: One leg straight, the other foot to the inner thigh, folding over the straight leg. Asymmetric, so both sides need it.

name: Headstand
description: Weight into the forearms, not the head. The traps and shoulders hold it up; the crown only touches down.

name: Hero Pose
description: Kneeling with the hips between the heels, sitting on a block if the knees complain. A quad and ankle stretch you sit in.

name: Heron Pose
description: One leg folded back, the other held straight up toward the face. An actively-held hamstring stretch rather than a passive fold.

name: Intense Side Stretch
description: Hips squared, folding over a straight front leg, hands in reverse prayer if the shoulders allow. Hamstring and shoulder at once.

name: Inverted Staff Pose
description: Wheel dropped onto the forearms with the crown down. Usually practised over a chair before it is practised on the floor.

name: Koundinya’s Pose
description: A twisted arm balance with the legs scissored front and back. Usually entered from Side Crow.

name: Legs-Up-the-Wall Pose
description: Legs vertical up a wall, hips at or near it. Five minutes does more than fifty seconds.

name: Lion Pose
description: Kneeling, tongue out, exhaling loudly with the gaze up. Genuinely a jaw, throat and neck release, however it looks.

name: Little Thunderbolt Pose
description: From kneeling, arching back until the crown reaches the floor and returning. Eccentric quad control, not flexibility.

name: Lizard Pose
description: Deep lunge with both hands inside the front foot, forearms down if they reach. The widest hip opener in a standing sequence.

name: Locust Pose
description: Face down, chest and legs lifted together, arms alongside. The plainest posterior-chain strengthener in the practice.

name: Lord of the Dance Pose
description: Standing backbend holding the lifted foot behind. A quad and hip-flexor stretch that has to be balanced on at the same time.

name: Lotus Pose
description: Both feet on the opposite thighs. It is an EXTERNAL HIP ROTATION, and forcing it from the knee is how knees get hurt.

name: Low Lunge
description: Back knee down, hips sinking, arms up. The front thigh works while the back one lengthens — both are true of "quads" here.

name: Low Plank Hold
description: Chaturanga held for time rather than passed through. The honest way to earn the transition in a vinyasa.

name: Marichi’s Pose III
description: One knee up, the opposite elbow outside it, the other leg straight. A sharper twist than Ardha Matsyendrasana.

name: Monkey Pose
description: The front splits. One leg’s hamstring and the other’s hip flexor at full length simultaneously.

name: Mountain Pose
description: Standing tall, feet grounded, weight even. Looks like nothing; it is the reference every standing pose is measured against.

name: Noose Pose
description: A deep squat twisted with the arms bound around the legs. Gated by ankle dorsiflexion long before it is gated by the twist.

name: One-Legged King Pigeon Pose
description: Front shin across, back leg long behind. Square the hips before folding — most of the depth people chase is just a twist.

name: Peacock Pose
description: Body horizontal, balanced on bent elbows pressed into the abdomen. Brutal on the wrists — build up slowly.

name: Pendant Pose
description: Knees hugged in, whole body swinging clear of the floor on the hands. The cleanest test of scapular strength in the practice.

name: Pigeon Pose
description: Kneeling backbend reaching the hands to the feet. The Ashtanga Kapotasana — not the one-legged hip opener of the same English name.

name: Plank Pose
description: One line from heel to crown, ribs knitted, hips neither sagging nor piked. Held on the hands.

name: Plough Pose
description: From Shoulderstand, feet over the head to the floor behind. A whole-posterior-chain stretch — never turn the head in it.

name: Prone Frog Pose
description: Prone, both feet pressed toward the outer hips. The strongest quadriceps stretch in the catalogue — keep the knees tracking.

name: Reclining Bound Angle Pose
description: Bound Angle lying down, ideally with the knees and spine supported. Held for minutes, not breaths.

name: Reclining Hand-to-Big-Toe Pose
description: On the back, one leg raised and held with a strap. The safest hamstring stretch there is — the floor keeps the pelvis honest.

name: Reclining Hero Pose
description: Hero Pose reclined back onto a bolster. A long, passive quadriceps and hip-flexor opener — never force the knees.

name: Reverse Warrior
description: From Warrior II, back arm down the rear leg and front arm overhead. A side bend held on a lunging base.

name: Revolved Abdomen Pose
description: On the back, straight legs lowered side to side under control. A twist that is genuinely oblique STRENGTH, not a release.

name: Revolved Half Moon Pose
description: Half Moon twisted toward the standing leg. A balance, a hamstring stretch and a twist with nothing to lean on.

name: Revolved Head-to-Knee Pose
description: Janu Shirshasana taken sideways rather than forward, top arm over the ear. A side bend and a twist together.

name: Revolved Side Angle Pose
description: Lunging twist with the opposite elbow outside the front knee. The back hip flexor opens while the waist rotates.

name: Revolved Triangle Pose
description: Standing twist over a straight front leg, hips level. Square the hips first — most of the depth people chase is a dropped hip.

name: Scorpion Pose
description: Forearm balance folded into a backbend, feet toward the head. A backbend and an inversion with no margin.

name: Seated Forward Bend
description: Legs straight, folding from the hips over them. Lengthen forward before folding down, or the lower back rounds first.

name: Shoulder-Pressing Pose
description: Thighs high on the upper arms, ankles crossed in front. Needs open hips as much as strong arms.

name: Shoulderstand
description: Vertical on the shoulders with the elbows in and hands supporting the back. Use a folded blanket under the shoulders.

name: Side Crane Pose
description: Crow with a deep twist, both knees stacked on one upper arm. Get the twist before trying to lift.

name: Side Plank Pose
description: Stacked on one hand and the outer edge of one foot, top arm reaching up. The bottom shoulder works as hard as the waist.

name: Sphinx Pose
description: Forearms down, chest lifted, hips heavy. The gentlest sustained backbend — good for long holds.

name: Staff Pose
description: Seated, legs straight, spine vertical, hands beside the hips. The seated equivalent of Mountain Pose, and just as easy to skip.

name: Standing Forward Bend
description: Fold from the hips with a soft knee and let the head hang. The point is the back of the legs, not the floor.

name: Straight Angle Pose
description: The side splits, legs straight out to either side. Adductor length, and years of it.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
description: On the back, knees dropped to one side, opposite arm wide. Needs no effort to hold — good at the end of a practice.

name: Three-Limbed Forward Bend
description: One leg folded back in Hero, the other straight, folding over the straight one. Quad stretch on one side, hamstring on the other.

name: Thunderbolt Pose
description: Kneeling, sitting back on the heels. The one seated pose traditionally practised straight after eating.

name: Tiger Pose
description: All fours with one leg extended and arched back. Anti-rotation work with a small backbend on top.

name: Tortoise Pose
description: Legs wide with the arms threaded underneath, chest to the floor. One of the deepest folds in the practice.

name: Tree Pose
description: One foot to the inner thigh or calf — never the knee. The standing leg’s glute medius does the balancing.

name: Triangle Pose
description: Straight legs, hinge sideways over the front leg. Length through both sides of the waist, not a collapse onto the front hand.

name: Upward Plank Pose
description: Face up, body in one line from heels to shoulders on hands and feet. The counter-pose to a long fold.

name: Upward Salute
description: Arms sweeping overhead from Mountain, ribs staying in. The first and last shape of the salutation.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
description: Thighs lifted off the floor, arms straight, chest through the shoulders. Not a cobra — only hands and feet touch down.

name: Warrior I
description: Front knee over the ankle, back heel down and turned in, arms overhead. The back hip opens while the front thigh holds.

name: Warrior II
description: Front thigh toward parallel, arms level, gaze over the front hand. The shoulders usually give out before the legs do.

name: Warrior III
description: Hinged to horizontal on one leg, one line from heel to fingertips. A single-leg hip hinge held still.

name: Wheel Pose
description: Full backbend pressing up from hands and feet. Needs open shoulders and hips before it needs a strong back.

name: Wide-Angle Seated Forward Bend
description: Legs wide, folding forward between them with the kneecaps facing up. Inner thigh and hamstring together.

name: Wide-Knee Frog Pose
description: Knees wide with the shins out and hips sinking back. Move in millimetres — the adductors object loudly to being rushed.

name: Wide-Legged Forward Bend
description: Feet wide and parallel, folding between them, crown toward the floor. Standing, but its work is the same as Upavishta Konasana.

name: Yogic Sleep Pose
description: On the back with both legs behind the head and the hands clasped under. Extreme hip and spinal flexion — go nowhere near it cold.

name: 90/90 Hip Rotation
description: Seated with both knees at right angles, rotating side to side. Internal and external hip rotation together.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rock
description: Knee driven forward past the toes with the heel down. What most people are missing at the bottom of a squat.

name: Backward Sled Drag
description: Walking backward against a sled — quad work with no eccentric, easy on the knees. Reps = metres.

name: Band Shoulder Dislocate
description: Band passed overhead and behind with straight arms. Widen the grip until it is easy, then narrow it.

name: Barbell High Pull
description: Hip snap into a high-elbow pull to chest height. Power for people who do not want to learn a catch.

name: Barbell Thruster
description: Front squat straight into an overhead press with no pause. The most exhausting barbell movement there is.

name: Bike Sprint Intervals
description: All-out efforts against heavy resistance, seated or standing. Reps = seconds per effort.

name: Box Jump
description: Explosive triple extension; step down, don’t jump down.

name: Cable External Rotation
description: Elbow pinned at the side, forearm rotated out. Light weight — this is a cuff exercise, not a delt one.

name: Clean and Jerk
description: Floor to shoulders, then overhead. Nearly every major muscle, in about three seconds.

name: Clean Pull
description: The clean without the catch — heavier than you can clean, and it trains the pull alone.

name: Couch Stretch
description: Rear shin up a wall, hips tucked under. The strongest hip-flexor and rectus femoris stretch. Reps = seconds.

name: Deep Squat Hold
description: Sit in the bottom of a bodyweight squat and stay there. Ankles, hips and back all at once. Reps = seconds.

name: Downward Dog
description: Hips high, heels reaching down. Posterior chain and shoulders at once. Reps = seconds.

name: Floor Press
description: Elbows stop at the floor, cutting the bottom range — shoulder-friendly lockout work.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
description: Knee flexion and hip extension in one rep on the GHD. Brutal, and the closest thing to a full hamstring lift.

name: Hang Clean
description: Starts from above the knee, so all the attention goes to the explosive second pull.

name: Hang Snatch
description: Snatch from above the knee — removes the floor and drills the turnover.

name: Hanging Oblique Raise
description: Knees raised to one side and then the other. Rotation added to the hanging knee raise.

name: Heavy Bag Work
description: Boxing rounds on the bag. Power comes from the hips rotating, not the arms. Reps = minutes per round.

name: High Row (Machine)
description: Downward-angled row path — sits between a pulldown and a row for the upper lats.

name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
description: Top pulleys swept down to the hips — lower-pec bias with constant tension.

name: Hill Sprint
description: The gradient limits stride length, which makes it much safer on the hamstrings than flat sprinting.

name: Incline Machine Press
description: Fixed-path incline press — upper chest without the stabilising demand.

name: Kettlebell Clean
description: Swing into the rack position. Guide the bell around the wrist rather than letting it flip onto it.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
description: The bell sits behind the wrist, so the shoulder works against a longer, less forgiving lever.

name: Kettlebell Snatch
description: One continuous swing to overhead lockout. The classic hard-style conditioning lift.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
description: Bell overhead, hinge sideways to touch the floor. Lateral trunk strength plus hip and thoracic range.

name: Landmine Rotation
description: Bar swept in an arc across the body with straight arms. Rotate the hips, not just the shoulders.

name: Lateral Bound
description: Push off one leg sideways and stick the landing on the other. Frontal-plane power and knee control.

name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
description: Cables from the bottom pulleys swept up and in — biases the upper (clavicular) pec fibres.

name: Machine Crunch
description: Seated ab machine. The most straightforwardly progressible piece of ab work in the gym.

name: Open-Book Thoracic Rotation
description: Side-lying, top arm swept open across the body. Mid-back rotation, which pressing and pulling both need.

name: Overhead Carry
description: Weight locked overhead, ribs down, walk. Shoulder stability and trunk bracing together. Reps = metres.

name: Pendulum Squat
description: Machine squat on an arc that keeps resistance heavy in the stretched position.

name: Pigeon Stretch
description: Front shin across the body, back leg long. Deep glute and external-rotator stretch. Reps = seconds.

name: Plate Pinch Hold
description: Two smooth plates pinched together and held. Thumb strength nothing else trains. Reps = seconds.

name: Plate-Loaded Chest Press (Iso-Lateral)
description: Hammer-Strength style: each arm on its own track, so a strong side cannot carry a weak one.

name: Plyometric Push-Up
description: Push hard enough to leave the floor. Upper-body power; land soft with bent elbows.

name: Power Clean
description: Floor to the front rack, caught above parallel. The classic whole-body power expression.

name: Power Snatch
description: Floor to overhead in one pull, wide grip, caught above parallel. The fastest lift there is.

name: Push Jerk
description: Dip, drive, and re-bend the knees to receive the bar overhead. Heavier than any press.

name: Ring Push-Up
description: Unstable rings force the cuff and serratus to work far harder than a floor push-up.

name: Rope Rear-Delt Row
description: Rope rowed to the collarbone with flared elbows — a face pull without the external rotation.

name: Seal Row
description: Chest on a raised bench with the bar hanging free — momentum and the lower back are impossible.

name: Single-Arm Cable Pushdown
description: One arm at a time, usually with a supinated grip — lets you work each side to the same standard.

name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
description: One side at a time through a longer range, with the trunk resisting the pull sideways.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
description: One foot down, hips squared. Bodyweight is plenty before adding load.

name: Single-Leg Press
description: One leg on the sled — evens out a side-to-side difference the two-leg version hides.

name: Sit-Up
description: Full trunk flexion off the floor. Feet unanchored keeps more of it on the abs.

name: Sled Push
description: Low drive position, no eccentric — hard work, easy recovery. Reps = metres.

name: Snatch Pull
description: Wide-grip pull to full extension. The long lever makes the back work harder than a clean pull.

name: Split Jerk
description: The competition jerk: feet split front and back to catch the bar with the biggest possible base.

name: Sprint Intervals
description: Maximal efforts with full recovery between. Hamstring-dominant — warm up properly. Reps = seconds per sprint.

name: Standing Broad Jump
description: Maximal horizontal jump from a standstill. Reset fully between reps — this is a power exercise, not conditioning.

name: Standing Hip Flexor Raise
description: Knee driven above hip height against a band or cable — trains the top of hip flexion, which sprinting needs.

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: Straighter knees than an RDL — more stretch, more lower-back demand.

name: Tibialis Raise
description: Toes pulled up against resistance — shin-splint prevention and ankle balance.

name: Toes to Bar
description: Hanging leg raise all the way to the bar. The lats have to stay engaged to control the swing.

name: Trap Bar Carry
description: Heavier than dumbbells allow, and the neutral handles keep the shoulders happy. Reps = metres.

name: Turkish Get-Up
description: Floor to standing with a bell locked overhead, then back down. Shoulder stability and trunk control in one slow rep.

name: Wall Ball
description: Front squat into a throw at a target. Squat and press fused into one very taxing rep.

name: Wall Slide
description: Forearms on the wall, slide up while keeping contact. Trains scapular upward rotation for overhead work.

name: Windshield Wiper
description: Legs swept side to side, hanging or lying. Rotation under a very long lever.

name: Wrist Roller
description: Roll a hanging weight up and back down on a bar. Reps = round trips; three is plenty.

name: Z-Press
description: Seated on the floor, legs straight — no leg drive at all, and the trunk must hold you upright.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: Anti-extension: fight the arch as the wheel rolls out. The lats pull it back.

name: Air Bike (Assault Bike)
description: Fan resistance rises with your effort, so it is self-limiting and merciless. Reps = minutes.

name: Arm Circles
description: Small to large circles both directions. Thirty seconds that make every pressing warm-up set feel better.

name: Arnold Press
description: Rotating press: palms start facing you, end facing forward — long delt time under tension.

name: Assisted Pull-Up (Machine or Band)
description: Counterweight or band takes part of your bodyweight — the honest route to a first pull-up.

name: Back Extension
description: 45° bench hinge — hinge at the hips for glutes, round-and-extend for erectors.

name: Band Pull-Apart
description: Arms straight, band pulled to the chest. Cheap, high-rep posture and shoulder-health work.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
description: Band above the knees, small side steps in a half squat. Warm-up or finisher for the glute medius.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: Bar on the upper back, hips below parallel. The lower-body benchmark.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: Bar to mid-chest, feet planted, shoulder blades pinned. The horizontal pressing benchmark.

name: Barbell Curl
description: Elbows at the sides, no swing. The basic loaded elbow flexion.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: Shoulders on a bench, bar over the hips, full lockout squeeze — peak glute tension.

name: Barbell Row
description: Hinged torso, bar to the lower ribs. The erectors hold the hinge isometrically.

name: Barbell Shrug
description: Straight up and down — no rolling. Upper-trap elevation under load.

name: Battle Ropes
description: Alternating or double waves from a quarter squat. Reps = seconds.

name: Bear Crawl
description: Knees an inch off the floor, opposite hand and foot moving together. Reps = metres.

name: Belt Squat
description: Load hangs from the hips, nothing on the spine — squat volume with the back fresh.

name: Bench Dip
description: Hands behind you on a bench. Easy to load with a plate, hard on the front of the shoulder — keep depth modest.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: Elbow to opposite knee, slow and controlled — flexion plus rotation.

name: Bird Dog
description: Opposite arm/leg extended from all fours without the hips rotating.

name: Box Squat
description: Sit back to a box, pause, drive up. Removes the stretch reflex and teaches hip drive.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: Rear foot elevated — brutal single-leg quad and glute work, hip abductors stabilise.

name: Burpee
description: Squat–plank–push-up–jump. Whole-body conditioning in one movement.

name: Cable Crunch
description: Kneeling, rope behind the head — the loadable, progressible crunch.

name: Cable Curl
description: Constant tension through the whole range, unlike free weights.

name: Cable Fly
description: Constant tension adduction; the triceps barely contribute, isolating the pecs.

name: Cable Front Raise
description: Front raise with tension at the bottom too, where a dumbbell version has none.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
description: Hip extension one leg at a time, squeezing at full extension.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: Constant tension from the bottom, unlike the dumbbell version.

name: Cable Pull-Through
description: Hinge with a rope between the legs — teaches hip drive with almost no spinal load.

name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
description: Neutral rope grip under constant cable tension — brachialis and brachioradialis work.

name: Cable Woodchopper
description: High-to-low diagonal chop, rotating from the hips. Loaded rotation, as opposed to anti-rotation.

name: Cat-Cow
description: On all fours, arch and round the spine slowly. Segmental spinal movement before you load it.

name: Chest Dip
description: Lean forward for chest bias; stay upright to shift load to the triceps.

name: Chest-Supported Row
description: The bench takes the lower back out of it entirely — pure upper-back pulling.

name: Child's Pose
description: Hips to heels, arms long. Lengthens the lats and the spinal extensors. Reps = seconds.

name: Chin-Up
description: Underhand grip — the biceps contribute much more than in a pull-up.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
description: Shoulder-width grip shifts pressing load from pecs to triceps.

name: Concentration Curl
description: Elbow braced on the inner thigh. Nothing else can help, which is the point.

name: Copenhagen Plank
description: Side plank with the top leg on a bench. The groin-injury prevention exercise. Reps = seconds.

name: Cossack Squat
description: Deep side-to-side squat with the trailing leg straight — strength at the end of the range.

name: Crunch
description: Ribs to pelvis, lower back staying down — short-range spinal flexion.

name: Cycling
description: Quad-dominant, joint-friendly conditioning. Reps field = minutes.

name: Dead Bug
description: Opposite arm/leg lowered with the lower back pressed flat throughout.

name: Dead Hang
description: Just hang from a bar with the shoulders active. Grip endurance and shoulder decompression. Reps = seconds.

name: Deadlift
description: Floor to lockout with a neutral spine. The heaviest whole-posterior-chain lift.

name: Decline Bench Press
description: Slight decline biases the sternal (lower) pec fibres; less shoulder involvement.

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
description: Lower-pec bias with the extra range and independent arms of dumbbells.

name: Decline Push-Up
description: Feet elevated — shifts load toward the upper chest and front delts.

name: Decline Sit-Up
description: Sit-up on a decline bench, easy to load with a plate on the chest.

name: Diamond Push-Up
description: Hands together under the chest — the hardest common push-up variation.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
description: Hinged at the hips with load on the hips — a long stretch on the gastrocnemius.

name: Dragon Flag
description: The whole body lowered as one rigid lever from the shoulders. Anti-extension at its hardest.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: Greater range of motion than the bar and each side works alone.

name: Dumbbell Curl
description: Supinating as you curl engages the biceps through both of its functions.

name: Dumbbell Fly
description: Slight elbow bend, stretch under control — loaded hardest at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: Lead with the elbows to shoulder height. The lateral-head isolation staple.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: One dumbbell arced back over the head. Loads the lats and pecs together at a long stretch.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
description: Dumbbells at the sides let the shoulders travel straight up without the bar in the way.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: One dumbbell, bend away and come back up. Loads the quadratus lumborum as much as the obliques.

name: Elliptical
description: Low-impact steady-state with light arm drive. Reps field = minutes.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
description: The angled bar semi-supinates the grip, which most wrists prefer to a straight bar.

name: Face Pull
description: Rope to the face with external rotation — rear delts, mid traps and cuff. Shoulder-health staple.

name: Flutter Kick
description: Small alternating leg kicks with the lower back pressed down. Reps = seconds.

name: Front Raise
description: Anterior-deltoid flexion to eye level. Sparingly — pressing covers this head.

name: Front Squat
description: Bar racked on the front delts keeps the torso upright — more quad, more core.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Floor version of the hip thrust — great activation warm-up or burnout.

name: Goblet Squat
description: Dumbbell held at the chest — the friendliest way to learn squat depth.

name: Good Morning
description: Barbell hip hinge from the back — start light, the lever arm is long.

name: Hack Squat
description: Machine squat on a fixed track — deep knee flexion, minimal balance demand.

name: Hammer Curl
description: Neutral grip biases brachialis and brachioradialis — thicker-arm work.

name: Handstand Push-Up
description: Inverted press against a wall. The hardest common bodyweight shoulder movement.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: The bent-knee regression — same pelvic tuck, shorter lever.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: Legs straight to horizontal, pelvis tucking at the top — the tuck is where the abs work.

name: High Knees
description: Running in place with the knees driven to hip height. Warm-up or interval filler. Reps = seconds.

name: Hip Abduction (Machine)
description: Glute medius/minimus — hip stability and width.

name: Hip Adduction (Machine)
description: Inner-thigh isolation; balances abduction work.

name: Hip Airplane
description: Hinged on one leg, rotating the pelvis open and closed. Hip rotation under balance — much harder than it looks.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: Lower back pressed flat, shoulders and legs off the floor. The gymnastics trunk position. Reps = seconds.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
description: 30–45° bench. Biases the clavicular (upper) pec fibres and anterior deltoid.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: Arms hanging behind the body on an incline bench — the long head under its deepest stretch.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: Upper-chest emphasis with a deep stretch at the bottom.

name: Incline Push-Up
description: Hands elevated on a bench or bar — the push-up regression that keeps the pattern intact.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
description: Steep grade at walking pace. High energy cost with almost no impact. Reps = minutes.

name: Inverted Row
description: Bodyweight row under a bar. Raise the feet to make it harder, walk them in to make it easier.

name: JM Press
description: Half close-grip press, half skull crusher — a powerlifting staple for bench lockout.

name: Jump Rope
description: Elastic ankle work at high cadence. Reps field = minutes.

name: Jump Squat
description: Bodyweight squat driven into a jump, landing soft. Low-cost lower-body power.

name: Jumping Jack
description: The universal warm-up. Gets the heart rate and the shoulders moving in one go. Reps = seconds.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: A hip SNAP, not a squat or a front raise — the bell floats off glute power.

name: L-Sit
description: Supported on the hands with the legs held out level. Reps = seconds; five is a real set.

name: Landmine Press
description: Angled bar press — shoulder-friendly arc between horizontal and vertical.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: Bar to the upper chest, elbows driven down and back.

name: Lateral Lunge
description: Step wide and sit into that hip. One of the few loaded movements in the frontal plane.

name: Leg Curl
description: Isolates knee flexion — the half of hamstring function hinges never train.

name: Leg Extension
description: Pure knee extension — the only way to fully shorten the rectus femoris under load.

name: Leg Press
description: Heavy quad loading with the spine supported.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
description: Toes on the edge of the sled. Heavy calf loading with the back fully supported.

name: Leg Swings
description: Front-to-back and side-to-side swings holding something solid. Dynamic hip range before squatting or running.

name: Lying Leg Curl
description: Face-down knee flexion. Keep the hips down — lifting them is how the range gets stolen.

name: Machine Chest Press
description: Fixed path — good for taking sets close to failure safely.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
description: Pads on the upper arms remove the grip and the swing — pure lateral-head abduction.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
description: Fixed arc against a pad — easy to run to failure and beyond with drop sets.

name: Machine Row (Iso-Lateral)
description: Chest-supported plate-loaded row — heavy back work with nothing asked of the spine.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
description: Fixed-path overhead press — easy to load and progress.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
description: Seated, fixed path — the safest way to take triceps work to genuine failure.

name: Meadows Row
description: Landmine bar rowed one-handed from a staggered stance — a big stretch at the bottom.

name: Mountain Climber
description: Plank position, knees driven alternately — core hold plus hip-flexor conditioning.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
description: Parallel handles — between a pull-up and a chin-up, and the kindest on the elbows.

name: Neutral-Grip Pulldown
description: Palms facing — the most shoulder-comfortable pulldown, with more biceps involvement.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: Eccentric lowering under bodyweight — the strongest hamstring stimulus known.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: Knee and hand braced on a bench — row to the hip, not the shoulder.

name: Overhead Press (Barbell)
description: Standing strict press. The traps and serratus upwardly rotate the scapula overhead.

name: Overhead Squat
description: Bar locked overhead through the whole squat. The most demanding mobility test in the gym.

name: Overhead Triceps Extension
description: Arms overhead puts the long head on stretch — best growth stimulus per rep.

name: Pallof Press
description: Anti-rotation: press a side cable straight out and refuse to twist.

name: Pec Deck
description: Machine fly. Pure pec adduction with the movement path fixed for you.

name: Pendlay Row
description: Every rep starts dead on the floor with a flat back — explosive, strict, no hip English.

name: Pike Push-Up
description: Hips high, head lowered between the hands — the bodyweight route to vertical pressing.

name: Pistol Squat
description: Full single-leg squat with the other leg held out front. Strength, balance and ankle range at once.

name: Plank
description: Rigid line from head to heels, glutes on, ribs down. Reps field = seconds.

name: Preacher Curl
description: Upper arms braced on the pad — no cheating, full stretch at the bottom.

name: Prone Y-Raise
description: Face down on an incline, arms raised into a Y — lower traps and rear delts together.

name: Pull-Up
description: Overhand, chin over the bar from a dead hang. The vertical pull benchmark.

name: Push Press
description: A shallow dip and leg drive launches the bar, so you can overload the top of the press.

name: Push-Up
description: Body in one line, elbows ~45°. The serratus works to protract at the top.

name: Rack Pull
description: Deadlift from knee height — overloads the top half and the traps.

name: Reverse Crunch
description: Knees pulled toward the chest with the pelvis curling off the floor — lower-ab bias without a bar.

name: Reverse Curl
description: Overhand-grip curl — wrist extensors and brachioradialis do the work.

name: Reverse Fly
description: Hinged or chest-supported, arms swept back — posterior-deltoid isolation.

name: Reverse Hyperextension
description: Torso fixed, legs swung up behind. Trains the erectors and glutes with the spine unloaded.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: Stepping back rather than forward is far kinder to the knees and more glute-dominant.

name: Reverse Pec Deck
description: Machine reverse fly. The easiest way to load the rear delts without hinging.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
description: The extension counterpart — balances heavy gripping work.

name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: Underhand grip drives the elbows closer to the body — lower lats and a lot of biceps.

name: Reverse-Grip Pushdown
description: Underhand grip shifts emphasis toward the medial head. Lighter than the standard version.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: Hips back, bar down the thighs, deep hamstring stretch — knees only slightly bent.

name: Rowing (Erg)
description: Legs–hips–arms sequence; ~60% of the stroke is leg drive. Reps = minutes.

name: Running
description: Steady-state or intervals. Reps field = minutes.

name: Russian Twist
description: Seated rotation with feet up — rotate the shoulders, not just the arms.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
description: Hang and pull the shoulders down without bending the elbows. Teaches the start of a real pull-up.

name: Scapular Push-Up
description: Plank position, elbows locked, only the shoulder blades move. Direct serratus anterior work.

name: Seated Barbell Shoulder Press
description: Back supported — takes the legs and hips out and leaves the press to the shoulders.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: Neutral grip to the stomach; squeeze the shoulder blades together.

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: Bent knees slacken the gastrocnemius, shifting the work to the soleus.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: Back supported, dumbbells pressed to lockout — anterior/lateral delt focus.

name: Seated Leg Curl
description: Hips flexed puts the hamstrings on stretch — better growth stimulus than the lying version.

name: Side Plank
description: Lateral trunk hold — obliques plus the down-side hip abductors. Reps = seconds.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
description: Bodyweight on one foot off a step — most people cannot do fifteen honest reps.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: Hinge on one leg with the other swinging back. The hip abductors fight the pelvis dropping.

name: Sissy Squat
description: Knees travel forward, hips stay extended — the deepest rectus femoris stretch under load.

name: Ski Erg
description: Double-pole skiing motion — upper-body-dominant conditioning that spares the legs. Reps = minutes.

name: Skull Crusher
description: Lying extension, bar lowered to the forehead with elbows still.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
description: Fixed bar path, no spotter needed — useful for pushing close to failure.

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: Fixed bar path with the feet forward — quad-biased and easy to fail safely.

name: Spider Curl
description: Chest on an incline, arms hanging straight down — hardest at the top of the curl.

name: Split Squat
description: Both feet on the floor in a static stance — the Bulgarian split squat without the balance tax.

name: Stair Climber
description: Continuous step-ups — lower-body conditioning. Reps field = minutes.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: Straight knees load the gastrocnemius. Full stretch at the bottom, pause at the top.

name: Step-Up
description: Drive through the top leg only — no push off the floor.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: Arms locked, cable swept to the thighs — lats without biceps involvement.

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: Wide stance, upright torso — more adductor and quad than a conventional pull.

name: Swimming (Freestyle)
description: Pull-dominant, zero-impact full-body work. Reps field = minutes.

name: T-Bar Row
description: Chest-high hinge over a landmine bar — heavy mid-back work.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
description: Handles at your sides keep the bar under your centre of mass — more quad, far less shear than a straight bar.

name: Triceps Kickback
description: Upper arm parallel to the floor, only the forearm moves. Peak tension at full lockout.

name: Triceps Pushdown
description: Elbows pinned to the sides, cable pressed to lockout.

name: Upright Row
description: Bar or rope pulled to chest height with high elbows. Keep it wide-grip and below the collarbone.

name: V-Up
description: Legs and torso meet over the hips. Keep the legs straight or it becomes a tuck crunch.

name: Walking Lunge
description: Long steps bias glutes; short steps bias quads.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
description: Belt or vest added once bodyweight sets pass ~10. The way vertical pulling keeps progressing.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: Wide overhand grip shortens the range and biases the upper lats over the biceps.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
description: Deep lunge, elbow to the instep, then rotate open. Covers most of what a warm-up needs in one drill.

name: Wrist Curl
description: Forearms on a bench, wrists flexed against the load.

name: Zottman Curl
description: Curl up supinated, rotate at the top, lower pronated — biceps up, forearm extensors down.
